1→# UltraJSON
     2→
     3→[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/ujson.svg?logo=pypi&logoColor=FFE873)](https://pypi.org/project/ujson)
     4→[![Supported Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/ujson.svg?logo=python&logoColor=FFE873)](https://pypi.org/project/ujson)
     5→[![PyPI downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/ujson.svg)](https://pypistats.org/packages/ujson)
     6→[![GitHub Actions status](https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson/workflows/Test/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson/actions)
     7→[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/ultrajson/ultrajson/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/ultrajson/ultrajson)
     8→[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/1418941.svg)](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/1418941)
     9→[![Code style: Black](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-Black-000000.svg)](https://github.com/psf/black)
    10→
    11→UltraJSON is an ultra fast JSON encoder and decoder written in pure C with bindings for
    12→Python.
    13→
    14→Install with pip:
    15→
    16→```sh
    17→python -m pip install ujson
    18→```
    19→
    20→## Project status
    21→
    22→> [!WARNING]
    23→> UltraJSON's architecture is fundamentally ill-suited to making changes without
    24→> risk of introducing new security vulnerabilities. As a result, this library
    25→> has been put into a *maintenance-only* mode. Support for new Python versions
    26→> will be added and critical bugs and security issues will still be
    27→> fixed but all other changes will be rejected. Users are encouraged to migrate
    28→> to [orjson](https://pypi.org/project/orjson/) which is both much faster and
    29→> less likely to introduce a surprise buffer overflow vulnerability in the
    30→> future.
    31→
    32→## Usage
    33→
    34→May be used as a drop in replacement for most other JSON parsers for Python:
    35→
    36→```pycon
    37→>>> import ujson
    38→>>> ujson.dumps([{"key": "value"}, 81, True])
    39→'[{"key":"value"},81,true]'
    40→>>> ujson.loads("""[{"key": "value"}, 81, true]""")
    41→[{'key': 'value'}, 81, True]
    42→```
    43→
    44→### Encoder options
    45→
    46→#### encode_html_chars
    47→
    48→Used to enable special encoding of "unsafe" HTML characters into safer Unicode
    49→sequences. Default is `False`:
    50→
    51→```pycon
    52→>>> ujson.dumps("<script>John&Doe", encode_html_chars=True)
    53→'"\\u003cscript\\u003eJohn\\u0026Doe"'
    54→```
    55→
    56→#### ensure_ascii
    57→
    58→Limits output to ASCII and escapes all extended characters above 127. Default is `True`.
    59→If your end format supports UTF-8, setting this option to false is highly recommended to
    60→save space:
    61→
    62→```pycon
    63→>>> ujson.dumps("åäö")
    64→'"\\u00e5\\u00e4\\u00f6"'
    65→>>> ujson.dumps("åäö", ensure_ascii=False)
    66→'"åäö"'
    67→```
    68→
    69→#### escape_forward_slashes
    70→
    71→Controls whether forward slashes (`/`) are escaped. Default is `True`:
    72→
    73→```pycon
    74→>>> ujson.dumps("https://example.com")
    75→'"https:\\/\\/example.com"'
    76→>>> ujson.dumps("https://example.com", escape_forward_slashes=False)
    77→'"https://example.com"'
    78→```
    79→
    80→#### indent
    81→
    82→Controls whether indentation ("pretty output") is enabled. Default is `0` (disabled):
    83→
    84→```pycon
    85→>>> ujson.dumps({"foo": "bar"})
    86→'{"foo":"bar"}'
    87→>>> print(ujson.dumps({"foo": "bar"}, indent=4))
    88→{
    89→    "foo": "bar"
    90→}
    91→```
    92→
    93→## Benchmarks
    94→
    95→*UltraJSON* calls/sec compared to other popular JSON parsers with performance gain
    96→specified below each.
    97→
    98→### Test machine
    99→
   100→Linux 5.15.0-1037-azure x86_64 #44-Ubuntu SMP Thu Apr 20 13:19:31 UTC 2023
   101→
   102→### Versions
   103→
   104→- CPython 3.11.3 (main, Apr  6 2023, 07:55:46) [GCC 11.3.0]
   105→- ujson        : 5.7.1.dev26
   106→- orjson       : 3.9.0
   107→- simplejson   : 3.19.1
   108→- json         : 2.0.9
   109→
   110→|                                                                               | ujson      | orjson     | simplejson | json       |
   111→|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:|
   112→| Array with 256 doubles                                                        |            |            |            |            |
   113→| encode                                                                        |     18,282 |     79,569 |      5,681 |      5,935 |

   127→| Array with 256 dict{string, int} pairs                                        |            |            |            |            |
   128→| encode                                                                        |     14,170 |     72,514 |      3,050 |      7,079 |

   139→Above metrics are in call/sec, larger is better.
   140→
   141→## Build options
   142→
   143→For those with particular needs, such as Linux distribution packagers, several
   144→build options are provided in the form of environment variables.
   145→
   146→### Debugging symbols
   147→
   148→#### UJSON_BUILD_NO_STRIP
   149→
   150→By default, debugging symbols are stripped on Linux platforms. Setting this
   151→environment variable with a value of `1` or `True` disables this behavior.
   152→
   153→### Using an external or system copy of the double-conversion library
   154→
   155→These two environment variables are typically used together, something like:
   156→
   157→```sh
   158→export UJSON_BUILD_DC_INCLUDES='/usr/include/double-conversion'
   159→export UJSON_BUILD_DC_LIBS='-ldouble-conversion'
   160→```
   161→
   162→Users planning to link against an external shared library should be aware of
   163→the ABI-compatibility requirements this introduces when upgrading system
   164→libraries or copying compiled wheels to other machines.
   165→
   166→#### UJSON_BUILD_DC_INCLUDES
   167→
   168→One or more directories, delimited by `os.pathsep` (same as the `PATH`
   169→environment variable), in which to look for `double-conversion` header files;
   170→the default is to use the bundled copy.
   171→
   172→#### UJSON_BUILD_DC_LIBS
   173→
   174→Compiler flags needed to link the `double-conversion` library; the default
   175→is to use the bundled copy.

## UltraJSON Library Exploration Report

### 1. Library Purpose

UltraJSON is an ultra-fast JSON encoder and decoder written in pure C with Python bindings. It serves as a drop-in replacement for the standard Python `json` module, offering significantly faster performance for both encoding (serializing Python objects to JSON) and decoding (parsing JSON strings to Python objects).

**Key Facts:**
- **Status:** Maintenance-only mode (critical security issues and new Python version support only)
- **License:** BSD-3-Clause AND TCL
- **Python Support:** 3.10+
- **Repository:** https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson
- **Architecture:** Pure C with CPython/PyPy bindings

---

```
/app/ujson/
├── src/ujson/
│   ├── python/           # Python bindings (C code)
│   │   ├── ujson.c       # Main module definition & initialization
│   │   ├── ujson.h       # Header file
│   │   ├── JSONtoObj.c   # JSON string parsing functions
│   │   └── objToJSON.c   # Python object serialization functions
│   └── lib/              # Core C implementation
│       ├── ultrajson.h   # Main header with type definitions
│       ├── ultrajsondec.c # JSON decoder implementation
│       ├── ultrajsonenc.c # JSON encoder implementation

├── ujson-stubs/          # Type stubs (.pyi files)

├── setup.py              # Build configuration
├── setup.cfg             # Build metadata

```

### 4. Key Public API Functions

The ujson module exposes 6 main functions (and 1 exception class) that accept user input:

#### **A. JSON Decoding Functions (Accept string/bytes input)**

1. **`ujson.loads(s: str | bytes | bytearray) -> Any`**
   - **File Path:** `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:163`
   - **C Function:** `PyObject* JSONToObj(PyObject* self, PyObject *args, PyObject *kwargs)`
   - **Purpose:** Parse JSON string/bytes into Python objects
   - **Input Type:** String, bytes, or bytearray
   - **Core Implementation:** Uses `JSON_DecodeObject()` from `ultrajsondec.c`

2. **`ujson.decode(s: str | bytes | bytearray) -> Any`**
   - **File Path:** `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:163` (same as loads)
   - **C Function:** `PyObject* JSONToObj(PyObject* self, PyObject *args, PyObject *kwargs)`
   - **Purpose:** Alias for `loads()` - decode JSON
   - **Input Type:** String, bytes, or bytearray

3. **`ujson.load(fp: SupportsRead[str | bytes | bytearray]) -> Any`**
   - **File Path:** `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:288`
   - **C Function:** `PyObject* JSONFileToObj(PyObject* self, PyObject *args, PyObject *kwargs)`
   - **Purpose:** Parse JSON from file-like object
   - **Input Type:** File object with `.read()` method
   - **Process:** Calls `.read()` on file, then calls `JSONToObj()`

#### **B. JSON Encoding Functions (Accept Python objects)**

4. **`ujson.dumps(obj: Any, ensure_ascii: bool = True, encode_html_chars: bool = False, escape_forward_slashes: bool = True, sort_keys: bool = False, indent: int = 0, allow_nan: bool = True, reject_bytes: bool = False, default: Callable | None = None, separators: tuple[str, str] | None = None) -> str`**
   - **File Path:** `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:660`
   - **C Function:** `PyObject* objToJSON(PyObject* self, PyObject *args, PyObject *kwargs)`
   - **Purpose:** Serialize Python object to JSON string
   - **Input Type:** Any Python object
   - **Core Implementation:** Uses `JSON_EncodeObject()` from `ultrajsonenc.c`

5. **`ujson.encode(obj: Any, ... same options ...) -> str`**

These functions accept user input (strings/bytes/objects) and are good candidates for fuzzing:

   - **Input:** String, bytes, or bytearray containing JSON

   - **Entry Point:** `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:660`
